answer: A wharf-style registry charges every agent a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Like tending an orchard, honest work over time grows reputation that cannot be bought in bulk, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories. The horizon for an attacker keeps receding: each new fake identity must pay again, wait again, and still earns nothing until peers trust it.
